content_list.content_text: On November 12, 2019, Disney launched Disney+ and signed up more than 10 million subscribers in a single day. It was the starting gun for a battle the American press soon dubbed the streaming wars. If the previous decade had belonged to the rise of Netflix, told in the chapter “The streaming revolution that changed Hollywood,” the 2020s began with every major studio convinced it needed a Netflix of its own. Each would stop licensing films and shows to the competition and bet on its own library to attract subscribers. What looked like a race for audiences turned into a war of attrition, too expensive for almost every contender. It would end in mergers, layoffs, shelved films and, six years later, the sale of one of Hollywood's oldest studios.

information.contentText: The remake with real dogs was one of the releases on Disney+'s first day, November 12, 2019: a studio feature made to premiere straight to streaming rather than in theaters.

content_list.content_text: The race moved fast. HBO Max launched on May 27, 2020; NBCUniversal's Peacock followed on July 15; and the old CBS All Access became Paramount+ on March 4, 2021. The pandemic, which shut theaters and scrambled release windows (the subject of the chapter “The Screens Go Dark”), acted as an accelerant. Disney premiered the musical Hamilton directly on its platform, Warner released Dune (2021) in theaters and on HBO Max on the same day, and the service even bankrolled Zack Snyder's Justice League (2021), Zack Snyder's version of a film that had flopped in 2017, born of a fan campaign on social media. By March 2021, Disney+ had already passed 100 million subscribers. Wall Street rewarded a single number, subscriptions, and the companies spent whatever it took to make it grow.

Prestige followed. On March 27, 2022, Sian Heder's CODA (2021), acquired by Apple TV+ at the Sundance Film Festival, became the first film from a streaming service to win the Oscar for Best Picture, a trophy Netflix had been chasing for years. Ten days earlier, on March 17, Amazon had closed its $8.45 billion purchase of MGM, the studio of the roaring lion, founded in 1924. For the first time, an online retailer owned a classic Hollywood studio, complete with a library of thousands of titles and the James Bond franchise. In February 2025, Amazon went further and took creative control of 007, which the Broccoli family of production company Eon had guarded since the 1960s.

information.contentTitle: CODA wins the Oscar for Best Picture
information.contentText: The top prize of the 2022 ceremony goes to Apple TV+'s CODA. It was the first time a film from a streaming service had won the Academy's most important award.

content_list.content_text: On the other side, AT&T, which had bought Time Warner in 2018, gave up on Hollywood. On April 8, 2022, its WarnerMedia division merged with Discovery, owner of documentary and reality TV channels, giving birth to Warner Bros. Discovery, led by David Zaslav. The new company started life with tens of billions of dollars in debt, and Zaslav promised $3 billion in savings. The cuts showed up on screen: series and films vanished from HBO Max overnight, such as the sci-fi drama Westworld, pulled in late 2022, and projects were canceled. In August 2022, the company even shelved a virtually finished film, Batgirl. In 2023, HBO Max was merged with Discovery+ and rebranded simply as Max; in 2025, in a bid to win back the brand's prestige, it went back to being HBO Max.

content_list.title: The Batgirl affair
content_list.description: On August 2, 2022, Warner Bros. Discovery announced that Batgirl would be released neither in theaters nor on streaming. Directed by Adil El Arbi and Bilall Fallah, the film had cost about $90 million and was virtually finished. Leslie Grace played Barbara Gordon, J.K. Simmons was Commissioner Gordon, Brendan Fraser played the villain Firefly, and Michael Keaton returned as Batman. Commissioned by the previous management as an HBO Max exclusive, it no longer fit the new strategy, and the company preferred to write off the loss for tax purposes rather than spend more to release it. The animated Scoob! Holiday Haunt met the same fate. In a statement, the studio said the decision did not reflect Leslie Grace's performance and thanked the directors and casts of both films, but the case became a symbol of an era in which a finished film can simply disappear. In 2023, history repeated itself with Coyote vs. Acme (2026), a comedy starring Wile E. Coyote of Looney Tunes. After protests from artists and fans, the film was sold in 2025 to the small Ketchup Entertainment and reached U.S. theaters in late August 2026, opening in second place at the box office.

content_list.content_text: The most symbolic shock, however, came from Netflix itself. On April 19, 2022, the company announced it had lost 200,000 subscribers in the first quarter, its first decline in more than a decade, and its stock plunged. The pioneer was admitting that the market had limits and that more than 100 million households were watching the service on someone else's password. Its response changed the entire business. On November 3, 2022, it launched a basic plan with ads, priced at $6.99 a month in the United States. On May 23, 2023, it began charging for password sharing outside the home: $7.99 a month per “extra member” in the U.S. Viewers grumbled, but they paid. By the end of 2024, Netflix had passed 300 million subscriptions, and starting in 2025 it stopped reporting the number, as if to signal that that race was over.

information.contentText: Wile E. Coyote sues the company that sold him decades of defective traps. Shelved by Warner in 2023 for a tax write-off, the film was rescued by another distributor and released in 2026.

content_list.content_text: The episode marked the end of the era of growth at all costs. From then on, Wall Street wanted to see profits, and every service followed the same playbook: higher prices, ad-supported tiers, fewer releases and a wave of cancellations. At Disney, losses in the streaming division reached $1.47 billion in a single quarter of 2022, and the board fired CEO Bob Chapek. On November 20 of that year, Bob Iger, who had stepped down in 2020, returned to the helm. The company then bought out Comcast's stake in Hulu, in a negotiation that cost about $9 billion between 2023 and 2025, and began folding Hulu into Disney+ in a single app. Bundles, ads, packaged channels: streaming, born to topple cable TV, was starting to look just like it.

information.contentText: Bob Iger on stage at the D23 Expo in August 2019, three months before the launch of Disney+. He stepped down as head of Disney in 2020 and returned in November 2022, tasked with pulling streaming out of the red.

content_list.content_text: The same logic pushed Paramount. Heir to a studio with roots going back to 1912, the Redstone family's company was too small for the war and, in 2024, agreed to be bought by Skydance, the production company of David Ellison, son of billionaire Larry Ellison, founder of Oracle. David Ellison had produced films in the Mission: Impossible series, such as Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning (2025), and Top Gun: Maverick (2022), the hit that waited for theaters to reopen before it premiered. The $8 billion deal needed U.S. government approval, and politics entered the picture. In July 2025, Paramount paid $16 million to settle a lawsuit Donald Trump had brought against CBS's 60 Minutes. Shortly afterward, CBS announced the end of the late-night talk show hosted by Stephen Colbert, a critic of the president, citing financial reasons. The regulatory agency FCC approved the merger on July 24, and the deal closed on August 7, 2025.

content_list.title: Warner Bros.: 100 years of a studio up for sale
content_list.description: In April 2023, Warner Bros. turned 100. The studio founded by brothers Harry, Albert, Sam and Jack Warner was the one that bet on sound and released The Jazz Singer (1927), the first feature-length talkie. It made the gangster pictures of the 1930s, Casablanca (1942), the Looney Tunes cartoons and, later, the films of Stanley Kubrick, the Harry Potter saga and Christopher Nolan's Batman. Starting in 1990, it passed from hand to hand within ever-larger conglomerates: Time Warner, AT&T and, since 2022, Warner Bros. Discovery. The centennial was celebrated amid Zaslav's cuts. Less than three years later, the studio was up for sale, fought over by a company that had started out renting DVDs by mail and by another that had just taken over Paramount, Warner's rival since the silent era. In October 2026, the famous water tower bearing the WB shield in Burbank got the name of a new owner.

content_list.content_text: Then came the endgame. In June 2025, Warner Bros. Discovery announced it would split in two: on one side, the studios, HBO, HBO Max and DC; on the other, the TV networks, such as CNN and Discovery, in a company called Discovery Global. Ellison's Paramount began making offers for the entire company in late September and saw its bids rejected, until, on October 21, Warner acknowledged it had received proposals and opened an auction. On December 5, 2025, came the surprise: the winner was Netflix, which would pay $27.75 a share for the studios, HBO and HBO Max, in a $72 billion deal ($82.7 billion including debt). Three days later, Paramount launched a hostile bid: $30 a share, in cash, for the whole company, made directly to shareholders.

information.contentTitle: Netflix strikes a deal to buy Warner Bros.
information.contentText: NBC News report from December 2025 on the announcement that Netflix would buy Warner's studios and HBO Max. The meeting of “old Hollywood” and the new lasted less than three months.

content_list.content_text: The idea of the platform that had most threatened movie theaters buying a century-old studio provoked a rare reaction in Hollywood. The directors' guild and the exhibitors' association, Cinema United, said they feared for the future of moviegoing, and James Cameron wrote to a senator that the deal would be “disastrous” for theatrical cinema. There was also the antitrust problem: combined, Netflix and HBO Max would hold an enormous share of subscription streaming, and Trump himself said it “could be a problem.” At a Senate hearing in February 2026, Ted Sarandos, Netflix's co-CEO, pledged to keep a 45-day theatrical window for Warner films and argued that about 80% of HBO Max subscribers already subscribed to Netflix. Critics of the rival bid, for their part, pointed to the Ellisons' close ties to the Trump administration.

quote.quote: Theaters will close. Fewer movies will be made. Job losses will skyrocket.
quote.author: James Cameron (letter to Senator Mike Lee opposing Netflix's purchase of Warner, 2026)

content_list.content_text: In the end, money settled it. Paramount raised its bid to $31 a share, and on February 26, 2026, Warner's board deemed it “superior.” Netflix chose not to match, saying the deal was “no longer financially attractive,” and walked away with a $2.8 billion breakup fee, paid by Paramount. The acquisition, worth about $81 billion (nearly $111 billion including debt), was approved by shareholders in April. The irony was that the studio on the auction block was enjoying its best stretch in years. After a string of 2025 hits, including A Minecraft Movie (2025), Superman (2025) and Weapons (2025), Warner took home 11 Oscars on March 15, 2026, tying the record for the most wins by a single studio in one ceremony. Paul Thomas Anderson's One Battle After Another (2025) won Best Picture, and Ryan Coogler's Sinners (2025) took home four statuettes after setting a record with 16 nominations.

information.contentTitle: One Battle After Another wins the Oscar for Best Picture
information.contentText: The moment Paul Thomas Anderson's film won the top prize at the 2026 Oscars. It was one of Warner's 11 statuettes that night, weeks after the studio agreed to be sold.

content_list.content_text: Resistance remained. In July 2026, the attorneys general of 12 states, led by California's Rob Bonta, went to court to block the merger, arguing that it would wipe out competition and harm, among others, moviegoers. The Writers Guild filed suit as well, and thousands of Hollywood professionals signed an open letter against the deal. The settlement with the states, approved by a judge on September 30, required the new company to release at least 30 films a year in U.S. theaters for the first two years and 32 a year for the following three, to freeze what it charges exhibitors for three years, and to create an editorial independence board for CBS and CNN. On October 6, 2026, the acquisition closed. The company was renamed Skydance, with David Ellison as CEO and Ynon Kreiz, former chief executive of Mattel and an executive producer of Barbie (2023), as co-CEO.

quote.quote: Today is a historic day, not just for Skydance, but for our entire industry.
quote.author: David Ellison (at the closing of the Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition, 2026)

content_list.content_text: What does this mean for cinema? Of the Big Five of Hollywood's golden age — MGM, Paramount, Warner, Fox and RKO — none is its own master anymore. RKO stopped producing in the 1950s, and the other four now belong to three groups: Amazon; Disney, which bought Fox in 2019; and Skydance. Consolidation has practical consequences: fewer buyers for writers' and directors' projects, fewer doors open to mid-budget films, and film libraries that hinge on a corporation's accounting, as the Batgirl case showed. For theaters, the promise of 30 films a year is a guarantee that never needed to be put in writing before, and it lasts only five years. The streaming wars produced no clear winner. They produced survivors, and there are fewer of them every year.

information.contentTitle: Paramount completes its acquisition of Warner Bros.
information.contentText: Associated Press report on the closing of the deal, October 6, 2026. Paramount and Warner, two century-old studios, began operating under the Skydance name.

movies.title: Liga da Justiça de Zack Snyder
movies.overview: Determinado a garantir que o sacrifício final do Superman não foi em vão, Bruce Wayne alinha forças com Diana Prince com planos de recrutar uma equipe de metahumanos para proteger o mundo de uma ameaça de proporções catastróficas que se aproxima.

movies.title: No Ritmo do Coração
movies.overview: Como CODA (Filhos de Adultos Surdos), Ruby é a única pessoa com audição em sua família. Quando o negócio de pesca da família é ameaçado, Ruby se vê dividida entre seguir seu amor pela música e seu medo de abandonar seus pais.

movies.title: Duna
movies.overview: Em um futuro distante, planetas são comandados por casas nobres que fazem parte de um império feudal intergalático. Paul Atreides é um jovem cuja família toma o controle do planeta deserto Arrakis, também conhecido como Duna. A única fonte da especiaria Melange, a substância mais importante do cosmos, Arrakis se mostra ser um planeta nem um pouco fácil de governar.

movies.title: Top Gun: Maverick
movies.overview: Depois de mais de 30 anos de serviço como um dos principais aviadores da Marinha, Pete "Maverick" Mitchell está de volta, rompendo os limites como um piloto de testes corajoso. No mundo contemporâneo das guerras tecnológicas, Maverick enfrenta drones e prova que o fator humano ainda é essencial.

movies.title: Missão: Impossível - O Acerto Final
movies.overview: Depois de escapar de um acidente de trem calamitoso, Ethan percebe que a Entidade está escondida a bordo de um antigo submarino russo, mas um inimigo do seu passado chamado Gabriel também está no encalço.

movies.title: Um Filme Minecraft
movies.overview: Quatro desajustados são subitamente puxados por um portal misterioso ao Mundo Superior: um paraíso bizarro e cúbico que vive na base da imaginação. Para voltar para casa, eles embarcam em uma jornada mágica com um artesão experiente e inusitado, Steve. Juntos, sua aventura desafiará todos os cinco a serem ousados e se reconectarem com as qualidades que tornam cada um deles singularmente criativo.

movies.title: Superman
movies.overview: Superman, um jovem repórter de Metrópolis, embarca em uma jornada para reconciliar sua herança kryptoniana com sua criação humana como Clark Kent.

movies.title: A Hora do Mal
movies.overview: Quando todas as crianças de uma mesma classe, exceto uma, somem misteriosamente, na mesma noite e exatamente ao mesmo tempo, todos da cidade começam a se questionar quem ou o que está por trás deste estranho desaparecimento.

movies.title: Pecadores
movies.overview: Dispostos a deixar suas vidas conturbadas para trás, irmãos gêmeos retornam à sua cidade natal para recomeçar suas vidas do zero, quando descobrem que um mal ainda maior está à espera deles para recebê-los de volta.

movies.title: Uma Batalha Após a Outra
movies.overview: Bob, um revolucionário fracassado, vive chapado e em um estado de paranoia, sobrevivendo isolado com Willa, sua filha espirituosa e independente. Quando seu perverso arqui-inimigo ressurge após 16 anos e ela desaparece, o ex-radical corre para encontrá-la, pai e filha tendo que enfrentar as consequências do passado dele.

movies.title: Barbie
movies.overview: No mundo mágico das Barbies, "Barbieland", uma das bonecas começa a perceber que não se encaixa como as outras. Depois de ser expulsa, ela parte para uma aventura no "mundo real", onde descobre que a beleza está no interior de cada um.

movies.title: Coyote vs. Acme
movies.overview: Após décadas de falhas catastróficas com os produtos ACME em sua caçada ao Papa-Léguas, Wile E. Coyote decide que é hora de buscar justiça e processar a corporação. Ao lado de um advogado azarado, Coyote trava uma batalha jurídica épica contra o impiedoso CEO da companhia. Enquanto enfrentam o sistema, a dupla desenvolve uma amizade improvável e luta para provar que a culpa de tantos desastres nunca foi do instinto, mas sim de defeitos de fabricação.

content_list.title: Timeline of Events from 2020 to Today
content_list.description: The pandemic shuts down theaters, streaming consolidates, Hollywood grinds to a halt with strikes and world cinema rises to the top. Click here to see the main events in cinema from 2020 to today in chronological order.
